title: Amsterdam Wisselbank
summary: The city-backed Wisselbank exchanged diverse coins for stable bank money and settled local and international payments by book entry.

parents.reason: The bank valued circulating coin and used a stable account unit to settle obligations.

title: London bankers' clearing house
summary: London bankers centralized daily exchange of cheques and bills, replacing clerks' repeated visits to each bank with net settlement among members.

parents.reason: Banks supplied the participating institutions whose interbank obligations the clearing house netted.
parents.directContribution: Member banks directly participated in daily multilateral settlement; this institutional coordination role is separate from the cheques and bills being exchanged.

parents.reason: Cheques and bills payable at member banks were the instruments exchanged and cleared through the London system.

title: FDIC established by 1933 Banking Act
summary: The 1933 Banking Act created the FDIC; the federal corporation began insuring covered bank deposits in 1934.

parents.reason: The insurance protects customer deposits held by banks and became part of the U.S. banking safety net.

title: BankAmericard network
summary: BankAmericard made revolving bank credit usable through a third-party card accepted by a broad network of merchants.

parents.reason: A bank issued and financed the revolving credit behind the card program.

title: Fedwire interbank transfer network
summary: The Federal Reserve linked its banks by telegraph so they could transfer funds electronically between member institutions.

parents.reason: The network moved funds among participating financial institutions' Federal Reserve accounts.
Telegraph lines carried the interbank transfer instructions connecting the Federal Reserve Banks.
parents.directContribution: Telegraph lines physically connected Reserve Banks; Morse code was the distinct message encoding carried over those lines.

parents.reason: The first network transmitted transfer messages using Morse code over its telegraph links.

title: Automated clearing houses
summary: Computer-based networks process batches of low-value bank transfers and direct debits, lowering the cost of routine payments.

parents.reason: Participating banks create and process the credit transfers and direct debits that the network clears.

title: Corporate university degrees
summary: Medieval European universities awarded formal qualifications, including Bologna's late-twelfth-century doctorate in civil law.

parents.reason: Corporate universities granted degrees that certified graduates' study and qualifications.

title: Research doctorate
summary: The reformed University of Berlin tied the Doctor of Philosophy to dissertation-based original research, establishing a research degree later adopted elsewhere.

parents.reason: The doctorate extended the university's existing system of formal academic qualifications.
Berlin's research-centered university reforms made original research and a dissertation requirements for the new degree.

title: Normal schools
summary: Dedicated normal schools prepare teachers in pedagogy and curriculum; an early French example was established by Jean-Baptiste de La Salle in Reims.

title: Monitorial instruction
summary: The Madras and Bell–Lancaster methods trained more advanced pupils to teach peers, allowing one schoolmaster to instruct large classes at low cost.

title: Jesuit Ratio Studiorum
summary: The Society of Jesus standardized a curriculum and teaching regulations for its schools across different regions.

parents.reason: The Jesuit order's growing school network needed shared rules for its officials and teachers.

title: Laboratory-oriented chemistry teaching
summary: Liebig's instruction at Giessen made supervised laboratory experimentation a method for teaching chemistry to university students.

parents.reason: University teaching provided the organized setting in which laboratory experiments became a repeatable part of chemistry instruction.

title: Royal Society of London
summary: A chartered learned society organized recurring meetings, experimental demonstrations, scientific papers, and scholarly exchange.

parents.reason: Natural philosophers meeting at Wadham College, part of the University of Oxford, supplied a documented setting and participants for the society’s formation.
Experimental inquiry gave the society a subject and practice for its meetings and demonstrations.

title: Philosophical Transactions
wiki: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society
summary: The Royal Society's journal established a continuing printed channel for registering, reviewing, disseminating, and archiving scientific claims.

parents.reason: The society's council licensed and reviewed the journal's monthly issues, while its secretary edited and published them.

title: Royal Society manuscript review
summary: The Royal Society's council required journal papers to be revised by society members before printing, an early framework for scholarly review rather than the later systematic anonymous process.

parents.reason: The journal's first publication rules required council licensing and member revision of submitted tracts.

title: Northcote–Trevelyan Report
summary: The report proposed merit-only appointments by examination and a permanent, politically neutral British civil service; these were recommendations, not the later implementation.

parents.reason: The report's authors were influenced by Chinese imperial examinations when recommending civil-service entry by merit and examination.

title: British merit-based civil-service recruitment
summary: A 1870 Order in Council implemented competitive, merit-based entry to Britain's permanent civil service, reducing reliance on patronage.

parents.reason: The Order in Council implemented the report's proposals for open recruitment and appointment on merit.

title: French Council of State established
summary: The Consulate established the Conseil d’État in 1799 as an executive council that advised on law and adjudicated claims against the state; the Restoration retained it as an administrative court, and an 1872 act later defined its role more precisely.

title: Peace of Augsburg
summary: The treaty gave Lutheranism legal standing beside Catholicism in the Holy Roman Empire and let territorial rulers choose between those confessions.

parents.reason: The Reformation's religious division and ensuing conflicts created the settlement's immediate problem.

title: Nicene Creed
summary: First adopted at Nicaea, the creed articulated shared Trinitarian doctrine for Christian communities that accepted its formulation.

parents.reason: The creed formulated doctrine within the Christian community and became a defining statement for Nicene Christianity.
